title: automated-proofworkflows-for-region-bound-controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and deliver an automated Proof Workflow that maps SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls to a catalog of evidence collectors, validates regional data residency constraints, enforces retention policies, and surfaces auditable artifacts to the Console and external auditors.

Scope:
- Control mapping layer that translates high-level SOC2/ISO controls into runnable evidence collectors (logs, ACL snapshots, KMS access records, config exports, RDS backups).
- Residency checker: for controls that require region-specific artifacts, verify source location, tag artifacts with region and residency status, and block cross-region export unless approved.
- Retention enforcer: automated TTLs and retention checks that ensure artifacts are kept for required windows and deleted/archived per policy.
- Artifact vault: secure store with immutable metadata, signer for integrity, and export endpoints for auditors (CSV export, signed bundles).
- Reporting & automation: scheduled evidence runs, ad-hoc collectors, webhook and SFTP export for enterprise auditors, and Console view with proof status and drift alerts.

Acceptance criteria:
1) A control-catalog PoC exists mapping 12 core SOC2/ISO controls to >=3 collector types each.
2) Residency checker can detect and tag artifacts as "in-region" or "out-of-region" for AWS/GCP regions in dedicated/private deployments.
3) Retention policies are configurable per-project and enforced automatically with audit log entries for deletions/archives.
4) Console UI shows proof status, last-run artifacts, and provides signed export bundles consumable by auditors.
5) End-to-end test demonstrating automated proof run for one customer with high residency requirements.

Non-goals: full coverage of all compliance frameworks (focus SOC2/ISO27001 first), long-term archival tier design (out of scope for initial delivery).

Tradeoffs & considerations:
- Tight residency enforcement increases operational complexity for private deployments; we'll surface a manual exception path requiring SRE/Compliance approval.
- Strong signing/immutability adds cost and storage; consider per-customer TTL defaults.
- Balance between real-time collectors vs. scheduled snapshots to limit performance impact on runtime services.

Integrations & dependencies: Console (for UI), Runtime infra for secure collectors (ENG-5022), Design for artifacts UX (DES-230), KMS/HSM and audit log pipelines, Dedicated/Private deployment templates.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1-2: Control catalog and collector spec; design review and security review.
- Week 3-4: Build residency checker and retention engine; prototype artifact vault (encrypted, signed).
- Week 5: Console integration, export endpoints, and final acceptance tests with 2 pilot customers.

Metrics of success:
- Reduction in manual evidence collection time from hours to minutes for pilot customers.
- 0 critical residency misclassifications in pilot.
- Positive auditor feedback on export bundles in at least one SOC2 engagement.
